title: Capability-anchored RBAC v2: temporal grants, audit-tag propagation, and admin safe-modes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: The current RBAC surface mixes coarse role bundles with resource-scoped permissions and lacks temporal constraints, making emergency elevation, short-lived admin tasks, and cross-service forensic tracing difficult. We also need a reliable mechanism to propagate request-level audit context (audit-tags) across downstream services so that security/observability teams can tie actions to SSO principals and transient grants.

Goal: Design a capability-centric RBAC v2 model that complements the existing scope/role hierarchy with: (1) first-class capabilities (fine-grained permissions), (2) grants that can be bound to resources and optionally time-boxed (start/expiry, TTL), (3) audit-tag propagation rules and mandatory audit metadata for elevated sessions, and (4) admin-safe modes (breakglass workflows, ephemeral elevation with MFA and recorded justification). The design must: articulate data model changes, API/SDK semantics, enforcement boundaries, migration approach for existing role bindings, SSO/SAML mapping recommendations (persistent roles vs ephemeral grants), and the audit log schema changes to support queryability across services.

Design notes (summary):
- Capability model: capabilities are the atomic actions (e.g., inference.run, model.create, tenant.link). Roles are collections of capabilities but can be deprecated over time; enforcement checks operate on capabilities.
- Grant objects: a grant ties a principal (user/service) to a capability at a specific resource scope (resource-id or hierarchical scope) with optional conditions: time-window (start, end), TTL, allowed-sources (IP, region), justification-string, and origin (SSO, API-key, service-account).
- Temporal constraints: system issues ephemeral grant tokens (signed JWT) for time-boxed grants. Default max TTL enforced by policy (e.g., 8h for admin-breakglass, 1h for standard ephemeral grants).
- Admin safe-modes: explicit breakglass flow requiring justification, enforced MFA, audit-tag injection, and automatic elevated-session recording. Admin sessions must create an audit anchor event and link subsequent actions via a single session-id propagated across services.
- Audit-tag propagation: require services to accept and forward sandboxed audit headers (X-RW-Audit-Session, X-RW-Principal, X-RW-Justification). The platform tracing/ingestion pipeline (console & observability) must index these fields and join events by session-id and principal.
- SSO/SAML mapping: recommend mapping IdP groups to role templates but prefer issuing ephemeral grants for high-privilege capabilities through SCIM or on-demand token exchange. For SAML SSO we should support an assertion extension that hints ephemeral elevation requests.
- Migration strategy: provide a migration assistant that scans existing role bindings, synthesizes capability-equivalent grants, and offers staged rollout (shadow enforcement -> read-only audit -> enforced) per tenant.

Implementation surfaces:
- Data model additions: capability, grant, grant_history (audit anchor), session_anchor_id (string).
- API changes: POST /grants to create ephemeral/permanent grants, PATCH /grants/{id} for TTL updates, GET /auth/check?capability=...&resource=... to evaluate. SDKs add a transientGrant helper for client-side flows.
- Console UX: add an Admin Elevation panel with justifications, TTL slider, list of active ephemeral grants, and searchable audit links.

Security considerations:
- All ephemeral grants must be signed and auditable; KMS-backed signing keys rotate.
- Breakglass flow requires mandatory manager approval if TTL exceeds policy threshold.
- Ensure audit headers are validated and cannot be forged by untrusted inbound requests (verify session-anchor signature).
acceptance_criteria: Data model RFC merged describing capability and grant entities and their fields
API endpoints for grant create/evaluate documented and prototyped
Console mockups for admin elevation and active grants reviewed by Design
Audit log schema updated; ingestion pipeline joins on session-anchor and surfaces in Console events view
SSO mapping guidance doc (SAML/SCIM) produced and security review completed
Migration assistant prototype can generate a mapping report for a sample tenant
Automated E2E test that proves ephemeral grant issuance, enforcement, and audit propagation across two microservices
